title: The Opening of the Season
sceneText:
The hunting ground is open country. The smell of the pine camp mixes with dung and leather. The banners hang slack; there is not enough autumn wind today to hold them.

Nobles and stewards are spread out between the fires and the tents. Baron Henk is at the centre of it, laughing among a group of hunters he knows. Marguerite sits in a folding chair with a half-closed book in her hand, looking elsewhere.

Further off, a party is mounting up. There are many more of them than there are here, and they are turned out differently: dark riding dress all matching, and the same device on the tack. Somebody in the middle of that party — at this distance all you can see is that she is laughing.

Somebody points her towards the tree line, and she nods. The whole party begins to move. In under a minute the Duke’s party is gone. From start to finish nobody looks over this way.

Henk sees you and waves.

{@henk}“Maplegate. You came.” He puts a hand on your shoulder. “Hartmann found a reason not to last year, and we had all assumed that estate was done with hunting for good.”

He steers you towards the fire.

Halfway there a man in a dark green coat comes round from behind a tent with a sheet of drawing paper covered in lines. He is giving instructions to two men behind him as he walks, and they are nodding.

Henk lets go of your shoulder.

{@henk}“Vallant,” he calls. “Which side are we starting today?”

{@thierry}“South-east.” The forester does not even look up. “That wind this morning has pressed the scent down low; the deer are below the slope. If you push from the north they will run out of the ground, and nobody is set that side.”

Henk is blank for half a second, and then laughs. “As you say.”

variants.thierry_met:
{@thierry}“Again, then,” he says. “I did say I am in the woods two hundred days of the year. These five are inside that.”

He opens the sheet out a little so that you can see it too.

{@thierry}“South-east today. If you are riding along, do not ride at the very front. That lot up there like to race, and when they race they do not watch the ground.”
variants.thierry_unmet: {@thierry}“Vallant. Forester, north district.” He folds the sheet away. “And you are the new steward at Maplegate.”

choices.text: Go with Henk to the fire

effects.logEntry: You went with Henk into the circle at the fire.

choices.resultText:
Henk takes you into the circle and names them one at a time. Two neighbouring landholders, a horse dealer up from Valehold, two stewards from other houses.

When he comes to you he says only “the new steward at Maplegate”. He does not give your name, and he does not say that you are a foreigner.

{@henk}“He has been here under a month,” he says, “and the books are straight already.”

Where he heard that, you cannot tell.

Somebody in the circle asks where you are from. You tell them. Somebody picks it up with a remark, and another man laughs.

Half an hour later you notice that you are listening to them talk about other things — whose horses, whose land, this year’s prices.

Nobody is asking you anything now.

choices.text: Pay your respects to Marguerite first

effects.logEntry: You went to pay your respects to Baroness Marguerite first.

choices.resultText:
You go over to the folding chair.

She does not look up. She closes the book first, and then looks at you.

{@marguerite}“You came,” she says. “Nobody came from Ludwig’s estate last year.”

She tilts her head towards the fire.

{@marguerite}“Henk is delighted. All last season he kept asking why nobody from Maplegate came.”

Marguerite sets the book on her knees.

{@marguerite}“He does not miss Hartmann. He just dislikes a place standing empty, when he knows who could have been sitting in it.”

choices.text: Stay where you are and watch how Thierry arranges it

effects.logEntry: You stayed where you were and watched the man in the green coat set out the day’s line.

choices.resultText:
You do not follow Henk straight away. You stay where you are and watch the man in the green coat.

He draws two more lines on the sheet, turns it round for the men beside him to see, says three sentences, and the two of them scatter to get on with it. The whole thing takes under a minute.

The man looks up and sees you watching him.

choices.text: Find somewhere out of the way to stand

effects.logEntry: You found a place at the edge of the camp and stayed there.

choices.resultText:
You find a place at the edge of the camp, against an unhitched cart.

You can see the whole field from here. Henk at the centre, Marguerite in her chair, the man in the green coat giving instructions. Attendants carrying the wine jars. Somebody lighting a fire, and somebody doing warm-up exercises with a good deal of show.

You stand there about a quarter of an hour and nobody comes over.

Nobody has come to find you today; standing at the edge was your own choice.

On the ride back at dusk Henk greeted you from the saddle, as warmly as he had in the morning.
